angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 862,668 km at 182.74 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.4723 +/- 0.0244 mas (same row, RUWE 0.95): 182.74 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.24 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Barragán et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-100 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.490..698B/abstract): 862,668 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.15 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Barragán et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-100 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.490..698B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5945 +/- 110 K from Barragán et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-100 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.490..698B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barragán et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-100 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.490..698B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-100.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.312, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
